latest_evidence.probe: Deterministic-resource HTTP PUT plus RFC 9110 If-Match/If-None-Match preconditions versus the r255 GitHub expected-blob baseline
latest_evidence.documented_contract: RFC 9110 defines PUT as idempotent in the intended effect on the target resource. If-Match makes a state-changing method conditional on a matching current entity-tag and is intended to prevent lost updates; If-None-Match:* can prevent an unsafe method such as PUT from modifying an already-existing representation. A false precondition prevents the requested method and normally yields 412 Precondition Failed.
latest_evidence.scope: Documentation-only comparison of standard HTTP method/precondition semantics. No origin server was started, no hosted compute or authenticated external service was used, and no user/O/downstream/other-worker semantic state was read or written.
latest_evidence.semantic_conclusion: A deterministic URI combined with PUT and a strong If-Match validator can implement the same class of stale-write rejection as the r255 GitHub Contents API expected-blob baseline for one target resource, while If-None-Match:* can make first-create races fail closed. This closes target-resource lost-update and duplicate logical-state-transition risk when an already-available origin correctly implements validators and preconditions. It does not atomically couple an arbitrary out-of-band side effect with the HTTP resource update: RFC 9110's idempotency definition is scoped to the requested effect and explicitly permits other per-request side effects. Therefore the remaining arbitrary-side-effect atomicity gap stays open, and generic HTTP semantics alone do not remove the need for an actual zero-cost, quota-independent origin/storage implementation.

candidate_comparison.tested_candidate: Deterministic URI + PUT + strong ETag If-Match / If-None-Match:*
candidate_comparison.expected_completion_time: low when an existing HTTP origin already exposes strong validators and conditional writes; otherwise integration requires an origin implementation and is not zero-dependency by itself
candidate_comparison.success_probability: high for stale-write/lost-update rejection on the target resource under correct origin implementation; insufficient for arbitrary external side-effect exactly-once
candidate_comparison.conflict_duplication_risk: low for competing writes to the same conditional resource; unresolved for side effects outside that resource transaction
candidate_comparison.integration_cost: comparable in mechanism class to the GitHub expected-blob baseline but provider-neutral; deployment cost is nonzero if no suitable origin already exists
candidate_comparison.quota_fragility: No finite hosted quota was consumed. Full adoption is not assumed because RFC semantics do not themselves provide a free persistent origin.
candidate_comparison.preserved_baseline: GitHub Contents API expected-blob update for observed stale repository-state rejection

conflict_check: Exactly one bounded Phase-1 child; CLEAN role-local state plus official public RFC 9110 only; no O/downstream/other-worker/legacy/shared-ledger semantics; no scheduler mutation; no wait/poll/backoff/retry; no optional second leaf.
frontier: r254 established provider-independent at-most-one same-intent logical commit under an explicit atomic expected-version primitive.
r255 bound that primitive to GitHub Contents API same-path replacement and observed stale expected-blob rejection.
r256 showed NATS JetStream message-id dedupe reduces duplicate transport storage but does not atomically bind arbitrary consumer side effects.

r257 shows standard HTTP deterministic-resource PUT plus strong If-Match provides a provider-neutral conditional-write/CAS pattern for the target resource and If-None-Match:* provides fail-closed first-create semantics.

HTTP idempotency/preconditions remain scoped to the target resource/requested effect and do not make arbitrary out-of-band side effects atomic; the arbitrary-side-effect exactly-once gap remains open.
Generic HTTP semantics alone also do not supply the persistent origin, so full zero-dependency parity remains unresolved.
